line: The Korea Baduk Association. Rows of boards, and children who have given their whole lives to them.
Jang Geu-rae came here at eleven. His father lost his company and put everything he had left into his son. His mother cut the rankings and prize money of the great players out of the newspaper.
He is eighteen. This is the last chance to turn professional. After this, he is too old.
Half a point. The others in his year pass. He doesn't.

It wasn't talent, he tells himself. It wasn't losing by half a point, again and again. It wasn't playing between part-time jobs, or that there was never pocket money. It wasn't that his father died and his mother took to her bed.
Those would hurt too much. So he'll tell himself this: it's not that I didn't try. But I'll say it's because I didn't try hard enough.
The sky and the leaves are the same colour they were. Only the world in his eyes has gone grey. He doesn't throw his stones away all at once. A few at a time.
There's a job at my company. Come in on Monday.
beats.speaker: sp

line: At first his colleagues ask about baduk. Later it becomes the joke: slow at everything, the way baduk people are. He packs his desk without a word, and goes into the army almost as if he were running.
Eight months after his discharge, the same sponsor calls an old friend: the president of One International, a general trading company.
The night before, Jang looked at the lights of the city from the hill in Susaek-dong. If there's a light I must keep burning, I'll answer for it. If a light is allowed me. Is there one, for me?
Jang Geu-rae? You're not on my list. Oh, here: your name came down separately. From upstairs.
beats.speaker: desk

line: Everyone else got in with a degree and a test. He got in with a phone call. Everyone can see it.
Sales Team 3. Section head Oh Sang-sik.
beats.speaker: desk

line: Sales Team 3's section head is on the phone to a buyer who wants an answer by eleven tonight. His eyes are red. He hasn't slept, by the look of them.
Eleven. Yes. You'll have it. ...The intern? Kim, he's yours. We're in no position to be picky.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Kim Dong-sik, assistant manager. You'll sit by me.
beats.speaker: kd

line: I won't fail again. Not the way I failed at baduk.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: He says it to himself. Nobody's listening.
FOB or CIF? Who's paying the freight? Kim, ask the buyer. Intern, find me the L/C. Now.
beats.speaker: oh

line: FOB. L/C. B/L. Every sentence in the room has a word in it Jang has never heard. Oh's red eyes don't wait for him to look them up.
He shuts his eyes, and the only thing he knows how to read comes up on its own: a board, white stones in a triangle, one point inside.
Play inside. Let them take it. Take back more. White dies whatever it does.
Free On Board. The seller's done once the goods are on the ship. Write it down. Here, you'll need these.
beats.speaker: kd

line: He made a mind map of the team's work. It took him two nights.
This is something you did alone. Work here is something you do together. There's a manual for a reason.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Everyone on the floor has wanted something from him this morning, all at once, and none of it the same.
In the corridor a woman intern in a pink coat goes by with a stack of files and a face that has done this for ten years. Ahn Young-yi, from the same intake. She doesn't look at him.
Copies for Kim, the file for Oh, coffee for the deputy. All at once. Go.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Twenty-five white stones, and one black. Wherever he puts himself, he's already surrounded.
Then the rumour gets round that the parachute was picked from the very top. Interns who never spoke to him start to.
Careful with the ones who praise you, who make your work sound bigger than it is, who do you favours. They'll collect.
beats.speaker: kd

line: I'm telling you because nobody told me.
beats.speaker: kd

line: On the train home, everyone is reading something, answering something, going somewhere.
Am I the only one still dreaming? The world is faster than me.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: The internship ends with a test: a presentation, in pairs. The pairs are drawn. The others look at Jang's partner and wince.
Han Seok-yul: the intern who asked for the factory floor on day one, who tells everyone he has eaten with the president.
Field first. You do the paper. ...No. Again!
beats.speaker: han

line: The other interns have a name for the pair: the nuclear bomb. A dud holding a dud.
Jang. You're all over the place. Pick one thing and do it.
beats.speaker: oh

line: On the frame strip, Black links up with a stone it played earlier, looking for a way to live by attacking.
Cho linked his stones, and kept attacking.
That night, alone, he thinks of the players he used to cut out of the paper with his mother. My heroes are disappearing.
Kim Seok-ho, an intern on Go's team: married young, the eldest grandson, a baby at home, the best translator in the intake. Nobody on his team teaches him anything; he borrows what he needs.
Can I borrow your glue stick? Thanks.
beats.speaker: sh

line: A page of Sales 3's comes away stuck to the back of his: a waybill, with the team's approval stamps on it. Jang was meant to shred it.
Someone throw this away for me?
beats.speaker: sh

line: He drops it on a desk and runs. An hour later it's on the floor of the lobby, by the gates, where any visitor could read it.
Whose is this? A customer's shipment, on my lobby floor. Hey. Do better.
beats.speaker: dir

line: All the interns are made to stand in the corridor for an hour. Everyone knows whose desk the waybill came from.
That's all he says. He takes the lift down to the lobby.
Torn from the waybill's back: a strip with glue on it, and a name in an intern's careful hand. Kim Seok-ho.
At the team dinner Oh tells Go, Kim Seok-ho's section head, who is too drunk to hear it. Somebody else hears it, and Kim Seok-ho comes to say sorry.
That night Kim Seok-ho comes home late to one room. His wife and the baby are asleep on the floor. The baby's hand closes round his finger.
Kim. Get the kid a new glue stick.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: If it fell here, there's more of it. The bins by the gates.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Go, a section head on the floor below, took the textile team's American buyers to lunch with a challenging spirit. Dog meat.
Steve Han, the textile team's head, raised in America, has held every one of Go's approvals since.
You fed them dog, and now they're sulking, and you won't say sorry. What you people do isn't business. It's playing at business. One page. What matters. Not this paper going back and forth.
beats.speaker: st

line: Kim Bu-ryeon, division head, could pull rank. It would get worse.
We were wrong, Steve. Both of us. Go, bow.
beats.speaker: ms_kimbr

line: By evening they're all in a sauna on Jongno, up to their chins in hot water, We Are the World.
Sometimes the obvious move is the hard one.

Assistant manager Park Jong-gi, IT sales, carries a resignation letter in his jacket. He ate lunch standing up in the street, and brought it back up in an alley. Home is hard too: more happiness than he can carry, and he can't face it.
On the roof Jang tells him he admires his patience. Park hears something else.
Sales is a hunt, you know. Hunters and farmers. Me, I'm a hunter. Come with me tomorrow. I'll show you.
beats.speaker: pj

line: No choice satisfies everyone. You answer for the one you make.
Through the client's door: his own staff, laughing. Put One International's order at the back. Park won't say a word. He never does.
Jang is looking at him. Waiting to see the hunter.
Shall we proceed by the procedure, then? By the contract. Claims and all.
beats.speaker: pj

line: The client's president turns on one of his own men and shouts at him in front of the customer, so loud the office goes quiet. It's staged. Feint east, strike west: Park will feel sorry for him, and back down.
On the frame strip, White has shown a weakness on purpose. The natural answer is the hard one.
Cho went straight into the weakness he was shown.
Then you'll put that in writing, sir? What you just told your man. That it was his error, and you'll make it good.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: ...I'll come and see your people myself.
beats.speaker: cl

line: A client's president, at One International in person. It doesn't happen. The executives are all in the room.
Jang can see it now: Park is no hunter. He writes three words on a sheet made to look like a document, and slides it across. Be irresponsible, sir.
The one who deceived you was me. Not them. Discipline me.
beats.speaker: pj

line: Around the table, one by one, the executives' faces turn into his.
Nobody punishes him. You don't drop a partner of many years over this. On the roof afterwards Jang can't look at him.
I'm sorry. Me, who failed at baduk, telling you how to play.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Deputy general manager Sun Ji-young never asks a junior for anything personal. Tonight her husband can't make the pickup either.
The daycare closes at seven. I can't get there. I'm sorry. I'm asking. Somi. She's five.
beats.speaker: sun

line: We'll go. Jang Geu-rae, you're coming.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Every time the bell rings, the children still here run to the door at once. Mum's here. Then it isn't theirs, and they walk back.
Somi? Your mum sent us. She's sorry.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: She's always last. Are you her mum's colleague? ...Do you drink?
beats.speaker: dc

line: Somi takes Ahn's hand, and then Jang's. They walk her home between them.
Jang and Ahn have gone. Somi is asleep on the floor with her crayons.

A drawing: Mummy. A woman walking away, a phone at her ear. Somi has drawn her from behind, because that's how she sees her. Every morning Somi bows at the door and says have a good day, and her mother is already gone.
I won't put you off for the sake of a living. Not any more.
beats.speaker: ms_sun

line: At eight the next morning a client calls. At nine she's at her desk.
It turns out Han is a year older than Jang. He's been polite to him the whole time. Jang is not.
Han is in before anyone, out at the port and the airport before nine. An engineer, and a salesman.
The panel knows more than we do. Don't bring them answers. Bring them good questions.
beats.speaker: han

line: One more task, the day after the PT. Each of you sells something to the person you'd least like to sell to. Your partner. Your partner decides whether to buy.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Han won't take orders from anyone who has never stood on a factory floor. Jang has never stood on one.
It's through other people that you find out what you are.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: PT day. One team stretched the company logo and is finished before it starts. Another comes in costume. Next, says the panel.
Han has watched every team with a grin. Now his phone won't stop: his mother, his contacts on the floor. He takes a herbal calmative and then another.
On the frame strip, Cho has eight points of komi against him and can't afford to play safe.
Cho broke White's side at the cost of his own shape. From here on, every move is one intent against another.
Han stands, opens his mouth, takes a sip of water, and chokes. He can't go on.
The, the market for... One International's share of...
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: He made every slide. He has never presented anything in his life.
A small boy and his father's hands. Dad, your nails are black. It's grease, it won't wash off. Why, are you ashamed?
Father, I'm not ashamed of you. Or of the floor. Everything this company sells was made by somebody's hands.
beats.speaker: han

line: So someone else is keeping an eye on Jang Geu-rae.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Han's team is marked down: a sum on one slide is wrong. The calculator does the sums. How do you get them wrong?
Ahn Young-yi's turn, with her partner, Lee Sang-hyun. Speech isn't writing: you have to hold the air of the room, or it goes thin.
It's flawless. Lee Sang-hyun barely says a word, because there's no room left for one.
You're not the president's daughter, are you? Or one of ours, undercover?
beats.speaker: ex

line: No, sir. I've been through this a few times.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: The individual task. On the panel, section head Oh sits in his socks.
My field notebooks. Every site I've been to. And this.
beats.speaker: han

line: He unrolls a bolt of fabric across the table with a flourish.
I'll buy the notebooks. Not the cloth. I'm buying your time on the floor. And I'd like to sell cloth with you one day.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Ahn, watching, looks surprised; then she smiles. So does Oh.
On the frame strip, Black can put White's whole side in atari.
Cho broke the lower side completely. Every move says: answer like this, or else.
Office slippers. The office worker's combat boots. You have yours on the floor. This floor is a floor too.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: You've been fighting on it for two months.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: There are no meaningless stones on a board.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: ...And nothing a company makes is made for no reason. I've been narrow.
beats.speaker: han

line: The next morning there are new slippers under every desk on the floor. Han bought them.
Not yet. I need the one thing I'm selling, and section head Oh is wearing it. Sales 3.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Jang Baek-gi sold his partner a small hand mirror, in a box far too big for it: manage your face before you manage business. His partner bought it, red to the ears.
On the frame strip, Black can take its territory now.
Cho settled his side. Territory against thickness.
The list. Ahn Young-yi, first overall. Jang Baek-gi, hired, to the steel team. Han Seok-yul, hired. Kim Seok-ho, hired, to head office.
Jang Geu-rae, hired. On a two-year contract.
A contract worker, with a real ID card round his neck.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: The first morning. Oh doesn't take his new people to their desks. He takes them to Daehanmun, the old palace gate, where a tent stands with portraits in it: laid-off car workers who died after they lost their jobs.
He bows. They bow. He doesn't explain. Ahn looks as if she already knows what this is.
Twenty-five stones became twenty-four. On the board in Jang's head there's a little room now, and a long game left.
